ob.tagline: Local-first vibecoding with Ollama – your code stays on your machine.
ob.how.title: How it works
ob.how.b1: Freevobe runs a local agent that reads and writes code in your project folders.
ob.how.b2: The model runs through Ollama on your machine. No code is sent anywhere unless you enable a cloud service yourself.
ob.how.b3: Every file change is shown as a diff before it is saved, and every command needs your approval.
ob.how.b4: No telemetry. No sign-in. No cloud account required.
ob.consent.local.title: I understand that the app reads and writes files locally.
ob.consent.local.hint: Sessions, memory and the project index are stored in a local SQLite database. You can delete everything from the settings.
ob.ollama.title: Connect Ollama
ob.ollama.body: Freevobe looks for http://localhost:11434 automatically. Start Ollama and press Check again if the list is empty.
ob.ollama.skipHint: You can skip this step and look around the app right away. Projects, the editor, skills and settings work without a model – only the chat waits for Ollama, and you can connect whenever you like.
ob.ollama.activeModelHint: Remembers the last model used per project.
ob.ollama.noToolsWarning: This model cannot call tools. The chat works, but the agent cannot read or change files. Pick a model with tool calling, for example qwen2.5-coder or llama3.1.
ob.ollama.unreachable: Ollama is not responding on localhost:11434.
ob.project.title: Choose a project
ob.project.body: Enter the path to the folder you want to work in. Freevobe indexes the code locally to find the right files.
ob.project.skip: You can skip this and open a project later.
ob.gives.title: Freevobe Gives Back
ob.gives.body: Instead of ads, Freevobe can remind you of a charity. It is entirely voluntary, off by default, and can be turned off at any time in the settings.
ob.gives.b1: The reminder appears in its own block, never as an AI answer.
ob.gives.b2: It never affects the model's answers, the context or the agent's decisions.
ob.gives.b3: No prompts, files or project details leave your machine.
ob.gives.b4: Freevobe does not accept money – you give directly on the organisation's own page.
ob.gives.b5: If you want to log a contribution it is stored only locally, marked as self-reported.
ob.gives.toggle: Show Gives Back after every 10th prompt (you can change the interval later)
ob.gives.footnote: Nothing happens if you skip this. The app works the same.
ob.done.title: Ready to forge
ob.done.t4: The Doctor button in the top bar checks Node, Git, Ollama, the model and permissions.
ob.done.autoUpdate: Auto-update is prepared but off until a release server is configured. See the TODO in the README.

permission.desc.auto-edit: File changes are saved after you have seen the diff. Commands require approval.
permission.desc.auto-run: File changes and commands run without questions. Dangerous commands are still blocked.
permission.desc.full-auto: The agent works on its own. Dangerous commands and writes outside the project are still blocked.
autoApprove.desc.file_write: Create, change and delete files in the project without asking.
autoApprove.desc.command: Run ordinary terminal commands without asking.
autoApprove.desc.test: Run the project's test command without asking.
autoApprove.desc.git: Create commits and switch branches without asking.
autoApprove.desc.network: Fetch web pages without asking (secrets are still blocked).

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.intro: Connect the services you already use. Every connector asks for the least it needs, shows exactly which permissions it wants before you connect, and can be disconnected in one click.
connectors.storage: Tokens are encrypted ({{cipher}}) at {{path}}. They never enter the model context and never leave this computer.
connectors.keychainOn: The encryption key is kept in your OS keychain.
connectors.keychainOff: The key is a local file readable only by you. Binding it to the OS keychain is the next hardening step.
connectors.noProject: Open a project to manage connectors
connectors.noProjectHint: Connectors are enabled per project, while the token is stored once for this computer.
connectors.git.name: Git
connectors.git.description: Local version control in the project, with status, diff, branches and commits. Built in – no key needed.
connectors.github.name: GitHub
connectors.github.description: Repositories, pull requests, issues and releases. Use a fine-grained token – never broad scopes.
connectors.vercel.name: Vercel
connectors.vercel.description: Preview deploys that show what is published, wait for your approval and then go live. Production always needs an extra yes.
connectors.supabase.name: Supabase
connectors.supabase.description: Projects, tables and SQL. Every SQL statement is shown before it runs, and writes need your approval.
connectors.netlify.name: Netlify
connectors.netlify.description: Sites and deploys. Coming soon – join the beta to try it first.
connectors.railway.name: Railway
connectors.stripe.name: Stripe
connectors.stripe.description: Read-only payments – no charges and no refunds. Coming soon.
connectors.resend.name: Resend
connectors.resend.description: Transactional email and domains. Coming soon.
connectors.cloudflare.name: Cloudflare
connectors.neon.name: Neon
connectors.neon.description: Postgres projects and branches. Coming soon.
connectors.toolsNote: Tools that change anything always need your approval. Production deploys have an extra step.
connectors.builtinNote: Runs locally in the project and is always available.
connectors.comingSoonHint: Shown for transparency; it cannot be connected yet.
connectors.scopes.title: Requested permissions
connectors.tokenHint: Pasted once. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
connectors.connectNote: The connection is stored now. It is verified against the service when the tools activate.
connectors.disconnectNote: Disconnecting deletes the token from this computer. Revoke it at the provider too if you want it invalidated completely.
connectors.revokedNone: {{name}} disconnected. There was no token to revoke.
connectors.openMcpHint: Connect any MCP server instead – its tools show up as regular agent tools.
connectors.toast.connected: {{name}} connected. The token is stored encrypted on this computer.
connectors.toast.disconnected: {{name}} disconnected. The token was deleted locally.
